summary: No. 3 Michigan beat No. 2 Ohio State 30-24 at Michigan Stadium for a third straight win in The Game, even after losing All-American guard Zak Zinter to a broken tibia and fibula. Acting coach Sherrone Moore called an aggressive game while Jim Harbaugh served a suspension over the sign-stealing scandal. The 12-0 Wolverines head to the Big Ten championship game against Iowa, aiming for a third straight College Football Playoff berth.
one_line: Michigan beat Ohio State 30-24 for a third straight year under acting coach Sherrone Moore, rallying after Zak Zinter's injury and Harbaugh's suspension.
key_facts: No. 3 Michigan beat No. 2 Ohio State 30-24, its third straight win over the Buckeyes in The Game; Michigan improved to 12-0 and Ohio State fell to 11-1.
Senior All-American guard Zak Zinter broke his tibia and fibula with 2:19 left in the third quarter of a tie game and was carted off.
On the next play, Blake Corum scored a 22-yard go-ahead touchdown and flashed Zinter's number "65" with his hands.
Michigan next plays No. 17 Iowa in the Big Ten championship game, seeking a third straight College Football Playoff berth.
Jim Harbaugh served a three-game Big Ten suspension over the illegal in-person scouting and sign-stealing operation; he returns Monday.
Acting coach Sherrone Moore called what J.J. McCarthy described as the most aggressive game he has ever called; Michigan converted three fourth-down attempts in the first half.
Corum scored on a one-yard touchdown run on fourth-and-goal for a 7-0 lead; it was his 21st rushing touchdown of the season.
J.J. McCarthy finished 16 of 20 for 148 yards and a TD, including a 22-yard touchdown pass to Roman Wilson for a 14-3 lead.
Will Johnson intercepted Kyle McCord with 7:32 left in the first quarter, setting up Michigan at the 7-yard line.
Ohio State's Jayden Fielding missed a 52-yard field goal wide left late in the first half; Ohio State tied it 17-17 with 6:08 left in the third quarter.
Michigan scored on every second-half drive with three field goals and a touchdown.
Safety Rod Moore, a Clayton, Ohio, product, sealed the game with an interception in the final minute.
Marvin Harrison Jr. had five catches for 118 yards and a TD for Ohio State.
Staffer Conor Stallions and assistant coach Chris Partridge are gone because of the scouting scandal, and the NCAA investigation continues.
Michigan lost in the CFP semifinals to Georgia and TCU in the last two years after winning the Big Ten title game.
